title: Why You Must Stop Selling Your Time for Money
key_points: Replacing a full human year of knowledge worker labor costs approximately $200,000 in AI tokens, and this cost is decreasing
Token economics means knowledge workers are increasingly in competition with the cost of AI tokens to do their job
The two hard problems every business must solve are speed to market (telling your story, letting people know you can achieve outcomes) and speed to value (delivering outcomes for customers)
Customers don't actually want to spend time with you - they want a particular outcome and currently think you're the fastest and cheapest way to get that result
A fitness trainer example: packaging GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic into fitness training offerings increases speed to value rather than competing against it

The agricultural age analogy: farmers did steps 1-2 (knowing when to plant, tending soil) and steps 9-10 (knowing when to harvest, taking to market), while soil automated steps 3-8 - AI will function similarly as digital soil
Five things you get paid for now: conviction, judgment, taste, commercial outcomes, and improving the system
Conviction is what fills you with life force energy and what you want to happen in the world - AI lacks conviction and is a total sycophant that reinforces what you want to hear
Judgment is about making good choices, having priorities, picking paths, figuring out questions to ask, which tools to leverage, who to bring onto a team - comes from experience and making mistakes
Taste is making creative choices aligned with ideal customer persona - requires spending time with your marketplace and picking up energy of ideal customers
Commercial outcomes covers making sales (getting people from unaware to clear, trusting, aware) and delivering results (transformation attributed to you)
The speaker's IT agency used to build WordPress online assessments charging $15,000-20,000 each, doing 4-10 per month
They converted that agency knowledge into ScoreApp (scoreapp.com), which now has tens of thousands of subscribing customers with AI-driven features
They also created bookmagic.ai from a publishing company's best thinking and a video production platform from a video production company
These platforms that used to be expensive and difficult to build now happen in weeks or months at most
The new role to play in a post-AI world is being a key person of influence for your business - being known, liked, trusted, and respected within your industry
summary:
The video opens with a stark warning that selling time for money through day rates, hourly rates, or monthly retainers is now dangerous. The speaker cites that replacing a full human year of knowledge worker labor (lawyers, professors, designers, editors) costs approximately $200,000 in AI tokens, and this cost is declining. This concept of token economics means anyone working in front of a computer is in direct competition with AI token costs.

The speaker introduces two fundamental business problems: speed to market and speed to value. Speed to value is delivering outcomes - customers don't want your time, they want results. The accountant example illustrates that clients aren't paying for time spent playing Scrabble, they're paying for tax issues resolved. A fitness trainer upset about GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic undermining their value could instead package those drugs into their offering, increasing speed to value. Speed to market is about telling your story and letting people know you can achieve outcomes - being on a massive podcast would explode a business because it rapidly increases market awareness.

An agricultural age analogy frames the coming shift: farmers performed steps 1-2 (knowing when to plant, preparing soil) and steps 9-10 (knowing when to harvest, taking to market), while the soil automated steps 3-8 (growing crops). AI functions as digital soil that will automate the middle steps, with humans responsible for initiation and completion phases.

The video details five things people will actually get paid for: conviction (what you want to see happen in the world - AI lacks this and is sycophantic), judgment (making good choices based on experience and refined through mistakes), taste (creative choices aligned with ideal customer personas, developed by spending time with your marketplace), commercial outcomes (making sales and delivering attributed results), and improving the system (staying current with tools and refining processes).

The speaker shares a concrete transformation example: his IT agency built WordPress online assessments for $15,000-20,000 each, completing 4-10 monthly. They recognized the real value was their strategy, conviction, judgment, and taste - so they coded ScoreApp (scoreapp.com), which now serves tens of thousands of subscribers with AI-driven features. They repeated this with bookmagic.ai from publishing expertise and a video production platform. These platforms now take weeks or months to build rather than being expensive and difficult. The video concludes positioning the new role as being a key person of influence - known, liked, trusted, and respected in your industry - and promotes a live workshop on this topic.
